newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - March 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - March 3.

text.p: The following were the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Police arrest two German nationals with boxes of rare snakes, lizards and frogs from house in Colombo suburb. The boxes were ready to be shipped abroad.
Government to put stop to import of onions and potatoes for rest of year to help local farmers, President Chandrika Kumaratunga tells election rally.
More than 520 incidents of election-related violence reported during past 25 days. A majority of complaints made by main opposition United National Party (UNP).
Local government election will be held as scheduled on March 21, Elections Commissioner Dayananda Dissanayake says.

Amnesty granted by police to politicians for handing in unlicenced guns expires tomorrow. Some 125 pistols and 40 guns have been handed over to police since the amnesty was announced on February 24, police say.
Colombo police chief D.M. Dissanayake warns of possible Tamil rebel attacks on election meetings, aimed at creating trouble in the country.
Parliament speaker K.B. Ratnayake calls second meeting of legislators on Tuesday to try and put a stop to rising election violence.
The Board of Investment (BOI) signs milti-million rupee agreement with two British universities to set up College of Clothing Technology in Sri Lanka.
Businessman Upali Dharmadasa elected president of Board of Control for Cricket in Sri Lanka for second year in row. Sri Lanka are the current world champions in limited-over cricket.
